notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware run. The package serves the simulated reaching environment only (R0) and has no hardware backend. The fake backend is the package's own kinematic pure Python stand-in (fake.py) for CoppeliaSim_UR5_gym_v3; it was not compared with the upstream environment, and the upstream simulator itself is not served: the clone registers no Gym environment id, imports its siblings as top-level modules from Simulation/, and needs CoppeliaSim, the legacy remoteApi client library at 127.0.0.1:19998 and a .ttt scene. The fake returns a 4x4x3 test image while the upstream observation_space is 128x128x3 (Simulation/CoppeliaSim_UR5_gym_v3.py:78-89); the real size is named in the fidelity gaps and here. The fake is kinematic (F0): no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuator, sensor, noise or camera rendering, and it was never compared with a real UR5. Its reset target is seeded with Python random.Random, whereas the upstream target draw uses numpy's global np.random.uniform and seed() only fills self.np_random, so the two do not share a seed stream. The real-robot part named in the repository README is not covered. The clone was read only and is unmodified. Warnings are the expected five of a Gymnasium family driver: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed is used by the next reset, not by a native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the derived integer inputs (ticks, action.values, seed twice). Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests.
